etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English panel (“piece of cloth, saddle pad, pane of glass, piece of ice, part, division, jury list, jury members”), from Anglo-Norman panel, panelle (“piece of cloth, saddle cushion”), from Vulgar Latin *pannellus, diminutive of Latin pannus (“cloth, rag, garment”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂n- (“fabric”). Cognate with Old English fana (“a piece of cloth, patch, banner, flag, vane”). Doublet of vane.

definitions.definition: (architecture) A sunken compartment with raised margins, moulded or otherwise, as in ceilings, wainscotings, etc.
A (usually) rectangular section of a surface, or of a covering or of a wall, fence etc.
A group of people gathered to judge, interview, discuss etc. as on a television or radio broadcast for example.

quote.citation: 2018, VOA Learning English > China's Melting Glacier Brings Visitors, Adds to Climate Concerns
quote.text: The United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recently reported that that rise is enough to melt 28 to 44 percent of glaciers worldwide.

definitions.definition: A portion of text or other material within a book, newspaper, web page, etc. set apart from the main body or separated by a border.
(comics) An individual frame or drawing in a comic.
(graphical user interface) A type of GUI widget, such as a control panel.
(law) A document containing the names of persons summoned as jurors by the sheriff.

quote.citation: 1765–1769, William Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, (please specify |book=I to IV), Oxford, Oxfordshire:  […]  Clarendon Press, →OCLC:
quote.text: To this end the sheriff returns his compulsive process , the writ of habeas corpora, or distringas , with the panel of jurors annexed, to the judge's officer in court.

definitions.definition: (law) The whole jury.
(Scots law) A prisoner arraigned for trial at the bar of a criminal court.

quote.citation: 1737, “Information for His Majesty’s Advocate, and Mr. Hugh Forbes, Advocate, Procurator Fiscal of the High Court of Admiralty, against Thomas McAdam, and James Long, Pannels”, in Extract of the Proceedings before James Graham of Airth, Esq; Judge of the High Court of Admiralty in Scotland, in the Action at the Instance of Duncan Forbes, Esq; His Majesty’s Advocate, and Mr. Hugh Forbes, Advocate, Procurator Fiscal of the Said High Court, against Thomas McAdams Souldier, and James Long Corporal, in the Regiment of Foot Commanded by Colonel —— Hamilton. Laid before the House Pursuant to Their Lordship’s Order April 18, 1737, London: Printed by John Baskett, […], →OCLC, page 12:
quote.text: [I]t remains only to examine the Relevancy of the two general exculpatory Defences pled for the Pannells.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) A piece of cloth serving as a saddle.

quote.citation: 1557 February 13 (Gregorian calendar), Thomas Tusser, A Hundreth Good Pointes of Husbandrie, London:  […]  Richard Tottel, →OCLC; republished London:  […]  Robert Triphook, […], and William Sancho, […], 1810, →OCLC:
quote.text: A panel and wanty, packsaddle and ped, with line to fetch litter, and halters for hed

definitions.definition: A soft pad beneath a saddletree to prevent chafing.
(joinery) A board having its edges inserted in the groove of a surrounding frame.
(masonry) One of the faces of a hewn stone.[1]
(masonry) A slab or plank of wood used instead of a canvas for painting on.
(mining) A heap of dressed ore.
(mining) One of the districts divided by pillars of extra size, into which a mine is laid off in one system of extracting coal.
(dressmaking) A plain strip or band, as of velvet or plush, placed at intervals lengthwise on the skirt of a dress, for ornament.
A portion of a framed structure between adjacent posts or struts, as in a bridge truss.
(British, historical) A list of doctors who could provide limited free healthcare prior to the introduction of the NHS.
(medicine) A group of tests or assays, a battery.

quote.citation: 1997, Michael Brodin, Encyclopedia of Medical Tests‎[1], page 270:
quote.text: This panel of tests can also help in cases where leukemia or lymphoma suddenly takes a turn for the worse (crisis) by determining if a change in the type of cells is causing the problem.

quote.citation: 2009, Rick Daniels, Delmar's Guide to Laboratory and Diagnostic Tests‎[2], page 478:
quote.text: A lipid panel measures three different types: low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and triglycerides.

definitions.definition: (obsolete, transitive) To enter (jury members) on an official list of jurors; to empanel. [16th–19th c.]
(obsolete, transitive) To fit (an animal, especially a mule or ass) with a panel or simple padded saddle. [16th–19th c.]

quote.citation: 1755, Miguel de Cervantes, translated by Tobias Smollett, Don Quixote, Volume One, II.5:
quote.text: The knight  […]  arose, and commanded Sancho to saddle his horse and pannel his ass immediately.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To fit (a room etc.) with panels. [from 17th c.]
